headline: 400 HSC scripts seized from teacher at tea stall in Sylhet
summary: A lecturer from Sylhet Metro City Women's College was caught grading exam papers at a tea shop with friends, leading to a formal investigation.
details: The Sylhet Education Board seized approximately 400 HSC exam scripts from a tea stall near the main gate of Shahjalal University of Science and Technology (SUST) on Saturday night.
caption:
Grading exam papers at a tea stall? 400 HSC scripts were seized from a lecturer in Sylhet.

The Sylhet Education Board seized approximately 400 HSC exam scripts from a tea stall near the main gate of Shahjalal University of Science and Technology (SUST) on Saturday night.

headline: 14,384 primary teacher recruits to join on Oct 1
summary: The Ministry of Primary and Mass Education has announced the joining date for selected candidates after eight months of waiting.
details: Nearly eight months after the final results were published, 14,384 candidates selected for assistant teacher posts at government primary schools are set to join on October 1.
The Ministry of Primary and Mass Education announced that selected candidates must report to the district primary education offices in their respective districts.
Appointment letters will be issued in due course, and recruits will receive their postings and undergo training after joining.
The recruitment process began with a nationwide written examination on January 9, involving 61 districts. A total of 69,265 candidates qualified for the viva voce.
Following the results published on February 8, selected candidates had staged demonstrations at Shahbagh and outside the DPE headquarters in Mirpur, demanding appointment letters.
During these protests, police allegedly baton-charged several candidates on April 27 while dispersing a sit-in outside the DPE headquarters.
In May, the Directorate of Primary Education began police verification of the selected candidates' documents and previous activities following a ministry directive.
caption:
14,384 new primary teachers are finally joining their posts on October 1.

Nearly eight months after the final results were published, 14,384 candidates selected for assistant teacher posts at government primary schools are set to join on October 1.

The Ministry of Primary and Mass Education announced that selected candidates must report to the district primary education offices in their respective districts.

Appointment letters will be issued in due course, and recruits will receive their postings and undergo training after joining.

The recruitment process began with a nationwide written examination on January 9, involving 61 districts. A total of 69,265 candidates qualified for the viva voce.

Following the results published on February 8, selected candidates had staged demonstrations at Shahbagh and outside the DPE headquarters in Mirpur, demanding appointment letters.

During these protests, police allegedly baton-charged several candidates on April 27 while dispersing a sit-in outside the DPE headquarters.

In May, the Directorate of Primary Education began police verification of the selected candidates' documents and previous activities following a ministry directive.

#Bangladesh #Education #PrimaryTeachers #JobNews #GovtJobs

Source: The Daily Star, Dhaka Tribune, Jamuna TV, Prothom Alo
